newsitem.title: USA: U.S. court orders Parretti to pay $1.5 billion.
newsitem.headline: U.S. court orders Parretti to pay $1.5 billion.

text.p: Fugitive Italian financier Giancarlo Parretti has to pay $1.5 billion following his conviction in a case related to the takeover of Hollywood studio MGM, a California court ruled Tuesday.

The court, upholding the terms of Parretti's bail agreement, ruled that Parretti, who is on the run from U.S. authorities, must pay the money to the CDR holding company, which took over the loan granted by French bank Credit Lyonnais to Parretti to buy the studio.

A Delaware court convicted Parretti last October of evidence tampering and perjury for altering a document that was used in a 1991 case stemming from Credit Lyonnais' takeover of MGM after Parretti defaulted on his loan.
Parretti had been scheduled for sentencing in that case in January, but he fled the United States for his native Italy and forfeited his bail.

A condition of his bail called for Parretti to pay $1.1 billion if he fled, according to Jay Coggan, Parretti's former attorney in Los Angeles where Parretti lived. The default judgment, issued Tuesday in Superior Court in Los Angeles, included the $1.1 billion plus $376 million in interest.
Coggan said the former movie studio head is currently in Italy, presumably living in Rome.
